insider_details.detail: For a wedding held in Australia, the notice of intended marriage goes to the authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the date, and it can be completed from overseas. Couples flying home for an Australian wedding can lodge it well ahead rather than leaving it to the final weeks. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.

Ask your celebrant early whether they appear on the Attorney-General's Department register of authorised celebrants (searchable by name and state), and which of the four types of authorised celebrant they are. A ceremony led by someone who is not authorised is not a legal marriage in Australia.

Plan the signing moment into the run sheet: 3 marriage certificates are signed on the day by the couple, the celebrant and 2 witnesses over 18, and the celebrant then lodges the paperwork with the registry in the state or territory of the wedding within 14 days. The certificate handed over on the day is ceremonial; the official one comes from the registry.

For a Whitsundays island date, ask the venue what its wet-weather option is for the summer months: Bureau of Meteorology averages for Hamilton Island Airport show January and February are far wetter, with many more rain days, than late winter and early spring. Describe the pattern; do not quote the figures.

For an outdoor ceremony in Australian sun, ask the venue what shade sits over the ceremony and guest seating, or whether you bring your own (shade structures or a sunshade tent). Cancer Council Australia recommends sun protection whenever UV reaches 3 or higher and says shade works alongside, not instead of, hats, covering clothing, sunglasses and SPF 50 or SPF50+ sunscreen reapplied every two hours.
